title: Seamless RBAC v2 Handoff: synthetic validation, org-consent flows, and operator rollback playbook
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket owns the operator-facing cutover orchestration for the RBAC v2 migration with three headline goals: (1) enable a dual-write + idempotent backfill pipeline, (2) provide deterministic synthetic validation and canary sampling at org scale, and (3) document transparent org-consent flows and rollback playbooks for production customers.

Scope:
- Dual-write shim behavior and invariants (v1 read, v2 write; shadow reconciliation)
- Backfill engine for historical role bindings with incremental checkpoints and progress metrics
- Canary plan: synthetic tenants + 1% real-traffic org cohort with opt-in consent flagging and throttles
- Audit-log preservation guarantees and event schema mapping v1 -> v2
- SSO/SAML mapping verification including NameID and group claim migration edge cases
- Operator runbooks for cutover, pause, rollback, and emergency admin bridge activation
- Customer comms templates and consent opt-in UX guidance for Console/CLI

Success criteria:
- Backfill completes for 90% of orgs within defined window (uptime/latency gates maintained)
- Canary cohort shows parity on auth success rate and no increase in 5xx auth errors
- Audit log parity validated for sampled tenants (event counts + canonical mapping)
- Rollback-tested in staging with <15m measurable recovery for affected requests

Acceptance tests / gating checks:
- Automated reconciliation job compares sample of 10k bindings between v1 and v2 with <=0.1% diff
- Synthetic traffic harness (synth-tenants) exercises SSO flows for common IdPs (Okta, ADFS, AzureAD)
- End-to-end SAML assertion test matrix executed in preprod with instrumentation enabled
- Console: admin role visibility parity and admin-bridge activation button functional test

Operational changes / runbooks to deliver:
- Cutover coordinator script (k8s job) to advance org waves and emit checkpoints to the rollout dashboard
- Runbook: Pause backfill -> safe rollback steps -> admin-bridge enable/disable -> postmortem checklist
- Dedicated SLO dashboard tile for RBAC v2 migration: per-org auth latency, error budget burn, backfill progress

Implementation notes / trade-offs considered:
- Dual-write model chosen to minimize customer impact but increases reconciliation complexity; mitigations: idempotent writes, monotonic version tokens, and a detection window to avoid flip-flop writes.
- Full immediate cutover would be simpler operationally but risks widespread auth disruption for customers with unusual SSO mappings.
- Staggered canary reduces blast radius at cost of longer migration time; chosen because RBAC touches many downstream systems (billing, audit).

Artifacts / links:
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.example/RBACv2-Migration-Playbook
- Design spec (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RBACv2-spec
- Canary dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.example/d/rbacv2-canary
- Backfill job repo (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-backfill
- Migration coordinator PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls?q=is%3Apr+rbac-v2

Notes for SSO mapping edge cases:
- NameID collision: add synthetic suffix mapping for downstream resolution; record mapping in audit event metadata.
- Group claim format variance: canonicalize to comma-separated group IDs during write; retain raw claim as additional field in audit logs.

Customer communications plan:
- Stakeholder wave 0: notify enterprise customers with dedicated CSM contacts two weeks prior; include opt-in instructions and expected windows.
- Public status: status.redwood.ai updates and migration FAQ two days before each wave.
- In-console banner for org admins with opt-in toggle and link to migration details + ability to schedule within a window.

Privacy & audit considerations:
- Audit logs must include original v1 event, canonicalized v2 event, and migration metadata (timestamp, generator id) to ensure forward/backward traceability.
- Retain dual-write tombstone for 90 days with access controls; include exportable CSV for customer compliance requests.

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Retention window length for dual-write tombstones (90 days proposed, awaiting legal approval)
- Exact cadence for automatic reconciliation (10m vs 1h); current plan: 30m checkpointing with adjustable backoff.
- Whether to expose reconciliation metrics to customers or keep internal-only (privacy vs transparency trade-off).
